subject: Pilot scoping & TCO summary — CobaltPayments discovery
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@cobaltpayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scoping & TCO summary — CobaltPayments discovery

Elena / Marcus — thanks again for a focused call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned while I pull the numbers together.

Summary of the call (short):
- Primary pain: user-facing fraud checks and reconciliation where current model endpoints cause spikes in token spend and occasional timeouts (mobile checkout).
- Business goal: cut inference spend while meeting 150ms median latency and 300ms 95th for confirmation path; pilot to validate 50% token reduction on day-to-day traffic.
- Constraint: procurement set internal pilot budget target to ~USD 25k/mo; decision window ~30 days for PO.

What we proposed on the call:
- 3-month pilot using a small dedicated pool (single-region, pre-warm) + prefix/KV caching and micro-batching for reconciliation flows.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost breakdown, cache hit rate metrics, per-route latency dashboards.
- Success criteria: >=40% net token savings, no customer-visible latency regressions, and measurable OPS simplicity (fewer retries).

TCO anchors (high level, attached):
- Baseline: your stated volume ~120M tokens/mo across the two high-volume flows.
- Expected pilot burn (Redwood) w/o levers: ~160k tokens/min peak => estimated hosted cost USD ~42k/mo.
- With batching + prefix caching + short KV cache TTLs we model a conservative 45–55% token reduction to ~18–23k USD/mo for the pilot. See attached tco_model_cobalt.xlsx for scenarios and sensitivity.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Elena — please confirm procurement contact and whether a vendor W9 or specific contract terms are needed (I attached initial TCO + one-pager).
2) Marcus — can you share a sample trace or a replay dataset (sanitized) for the checkout path? A small sample will let us validate cache-hit assumptions.
3) Redwood (Ben/Marissa) — we’ll deliver a 1-page pilot SOW and a cost table (unit cost per 1k tokens across three plan scenarios) by EOD Thursday (PST).

Attachments: [attachment: cobalt_tco_summary.pdf (PDF, 92KB)], [attachment: tco_model_cobalt.xlsx (Excel, 210KB)].

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the SOW draft and the cost sensitivity table.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.com

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@cobaltpayments.com>

Cc: Marcus Low <marcus.low@cobaltpayments.com>, procurement@cobaltpayments.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 20:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Pilot scoping & TCO summary — CobaltPayments discovery

Thanks, Nikhil — helpful summary and appreciated the sensitivity workbook. A few quick notes: 

On budget & timeline:
- We’re aligned on the ~USD 25k/mo constraint for an initial pilot; Procurement needs an estimate line itemized (monthly license / service + infra delta + one-time setup). Our PO cycle is ~30 days.

On security:
- We’ll need Redwood’s SOC2 report and any standard DPA language for PCI-adjacent workloads. Marcus copied me with the sample traces request — we can send a sanitized replay but need a short NDA addendum (we can do that through procurement).

On technical asks (please include in your SOW):
- A table with expected p95 latency impact per route (baseline vs pilot with batching) and the fallback behavior for cold cache misses.
- Unit cost per 1k tokens (three scenarios: conservative, mid, optimistic) + how that maps to ~120M tokens/mo.

Procurement contact: procurement@cobaltpayments.com (they’re CC’d). I’m looping them in so they can request vendor forms; they’ll also confirm PO terms.

Elena
VP Product — CobaltPayments
